assumptions.density_area_note: Uses DESI DR1 approximate Main Survey dark-program area as a deliberately coarse normalization. This is not a substitute for tracer-specific clustering masks/effective volume.
assumptions.claim_boundary: Cross-survey comparisons with different selections, tracers and redshift regimes are treated as orthogonal consistency checks, not pooled confirmation.

tests.name: DESI_NZ_SAMPLE_CONTRACT
evidence: DESI DR1 publishes tracer redshift distributions for ELG/LRG/BGS/QSO and an approximate dark-program area of 9528 deg2.
Published DESI clustering sample definitions report LRG 0.4<z<1.1, ELG 0.8<z<1.6 and primary QSO clustering 0.8<z<2.1, with tracer-specific success criteria.

tests.name: COMOVING_DENSITY_SANITY
tests.method: N/Vshell using flat LambdaCDM and the approximate 9528 deg2 DR1 dark-program area; counts/ranges from published clustering-sample summary.
tests.interpretation: Ordering is physically plausible for the progressively rarer tracer populations. Values are sanity checks only because the real clustering masks, completeness weights and n(z) structure are tracer/redshift dependent.

tests.name: CLUSTERING_BIAS_CONSISTENCY
tests.evidence: DESI One-Percent HOD analysis reports LRG linear bias 1.93 (+0.06/-0.04) at z=0.4-0.6 and 2.08 +/-0.03 at z=0.6-0.8, while QSO bias is 2.63 (+0.37/-0.26) over z=0.8-2.1. The hierarchy is consistent with increasingly biased rarer tracers and shows no obvious contradiction with the coarse-density ordering.
tests.boundary: This is a consistency bridge from the validated One-Percent HOD analysis, not a replacement for a DR1 tracer-by-tracer bias refit.

tests.name: EUCLID_DIRECT_CROSSCHECK
tests.evidence: Euclid Q1 released 63.1 deg2 and ~26 million detections but is explicitly not a cosmology release. ESA states the first cosmology data release is planned for October 2026.
tests.interpretation: No negative scientific verdict. Direct DESI-vs-Euclid cosmological N(z)/clustering validation is premature at this run date.

tests.name: COSMOS_WEB_HIGHZ_DENSITY_BRIDGE
tests.evidence: COSMOS-Web LSS uses ~164k galaxies over 0.54 deg2 with photo-z quality sigma_z/(1+z)<0.1 and traces density structure to high redshift; this independently demonstrates measurable environment/density structure outside the DESI spectroscopic regime.
tests.boundary: Small-area photometric selection and different tracer population prohibit treating this as a direct normalization of DESI N(z) or bias.

tests.name: JWST_HIGHZ_ABUNDANCE_BOUNDARY
tests.evidence: COSMOS-Web UVLF work reports 3099 galaxies across z~5.5-14 and a bright-end excess beginning around z~9, increasing toward z~12. Independent spectroscopy in GLASS confirms a high z~10 abundance and notes clustering and AGN contamination as viable contributors.
tests.interpretation: High-z abundance remains a real modeling target, but the current evidence does not uniquely identify cosmology because star-formation efficiency, stochasticity, dust, AGN contamination and cosmic structure remain live explanations.

summary.scientific_close: DESI N(z), coarse density and bias are mutually consistent at sanity-check level. COSMOS-Web/JWST strengthens the case that high-z abundance and environment require explicit selection/astrophysical modeling. Euclid cannot yet serve as a direct cosmology cross-check before its core cosmology release.
